findings.where: Explain text, second paragraph ("Textbooks add that a beam's bending moment at a point is the turning effect ... of everything on one side of it")
findings.what: The definition of a bending moment, and the rule that a spread load acts at its middle, have no footnote, and "Textbooks add" makes an unsourced claim look sourced. The brief required the research stage to cite what a moment is and M = wx(L − x) ÷ 2 before the lesson states them, but research notes 7.3 has only "My reading". Cite a statics source for the definition, or label it as the lesson's own working.

It says the support's push "turns the beam 6x kN·m one way" but never says the turning effects are taken about the point, counting only what lies to its left. Add that clause, so Dan sees why the right support's push (drawn in grey) does not count.

"Slide the current" never says what sets the current in a real circuit, the load's resistance through I = E ÷ (r + R). That only appears in screen 8's working. One clause on screen 5 (each load sets a current, so sliding the current is choosing the load) would prepare both the "load equals r" result and screen 8.

findings.where: Screen 8 (Double the load), right working and the 144 W wrong pick
findings.what: 12 ÷ (0.5 + 1) is used without saying the load and r are in series, 1.5 Ω in all. Also, the red ring for 144 W lands on the navy "battery makes" line at 12 A, because 12² × 1 and 12 × 12 happen to be equal, so it can read as "what the battery makes" rather than "the old current kept".

findings.where: Screen 8 (Double the load), Why?, or screen 7
findings.what: The power-against-efficiency trade is told from one side only: at the match half is lost. Screen 8 already has the other side. At 1 Ω the load gets 64 W of the 96 W made, about two-thirds, so it gets less power but loses less. Say that in one line, so the caution becomes the trade an electrician actually makes.
All three answers begin "3 m", so the buttons answer the "where" half of the question. Either drop "where" from the task, or give one wrong pick a wrong place, such as "4 m, 8 kN·m" (24 − 16 = 8).

findings.where: Screen 13 (A shorter beam), question row and the 18 kN·m pick
findings.what: The question row already gives "Each support holds 6 kN, so M = 6x − 1.5x²", so the 18 kN·m pick (one support holding all 12 kN) contradicts the given line and tests nothing. Either let Dan build the rule himself, or replace 18 with a slip that can be reached from the given rule.

findings.where: Ball / Supply / Beam pills at the top of every screen
findings.what: They are drawn like a selected switch but do nothing: they are aria-hidden and have no handler, and the brief's "switch between three jobs" is not a switch Dan can use. Style them as plain labels, or make a tap jump to that job's first screen.

findings.where: Lead paragraph above the stepper (seen on the step 13 end screenshot)
findings.what: Every screen repeats "a 6 m beam carrying 2 kN on every metre" and the first ball and battery figures, including screens 4, 11, 12 and 13, which use other example figures. On screen 13 it sits above a 4 m beam carrying 3 kN on every metre. Say "Example figures throughout" instead of listing them.

findings.where: Screen 1 readouts (also screens 5 and 9 when moved)
findings.what: The rows show three decimals, for example "4.9 × 1.2² = 7.056 m" and "23.52 − 7.056 = 16.464 m". A thrown ball's height to the millimetre is noise for Dan. Two decimals (23.52 − 7.06 = 16.46) still add up and read more calmly.

The time axis ends exactly at 4 s, so the two parts meet in the plot's top-right corner, and 4 s can be read off the end of the axis instead of from 19.6t = 4.9t². Run the axis a little past 4 s, drawing only the two parts, so the crossing sits inside the plot.

findings.where: Lesson as a whole, compared with the brief
findings.what: The brief promises every lesson a "spot the slip" screen, and lesson 7 has none, though the red working on each wrong pick covers similar ground. A worked answer that keeps −1 s, or that puts the deck ball's top at 1 s, with "which line slips?" would keep the promise.

The bold 1.2rem question is about 45 words long and restates the rule that the question row already shows. Keep the bold task to the setting and the question, and leave h = 9.8 + 4.9t − 4.9t² and "drawn dashed before the throw" to the working lines.
